answer.evidence: The awning spans rows 3-19 as a sloped canopy plane. Its stripes run from the light upper rows (4-11) to the darker lower rows (12-18), and a dark outline at row 19 closes it as the front edge. That is evidence (c). The counter below has a front face at rows 30-44 (about 15 rows) with plank lines and a door opening. Its top is only a 2-row lighter strip at rows 28-29, which is a rim and not a real top surface. The posts at the sides are vertical faces. There is no isometric side face. Because the awning gives a large top surface above a tall front face, the drawing reads as three_quarter, although the counter top is thin.

Measured facts: 9 visible tones per tile against 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the well. Near-flat coverage is 21% against 13% and 0%, so it is flatter than the same-kind reference. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted dark red-brown rather than a black sticker line, which is good. Shading is shallow: the awning stripes carry about 3 tones, and the wood counter and dark interior are mostly flat blocks of 1-2 tones. They lack the per-plank grain, the hanging goods and the clutter that the cheese stall has. The stripes and some tattered edge detail give it some character. Overall it is acceptable in structure but noticeably flatter and sparser than the cheese stall, with larger flat areas in the dark opening and the counter front, so it falls short of the Beodeul bar.
